D001039.s: An aphasia characterized by impairment of expressive language (speech, writing, signs) and relative preservation of receptive language abilities (i.e., comprehension).

D001310.s: An oral chrysotherapeutic agent for the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis. Its exact mechanism of action is unknown, but it is believed to act via immunological mechanisms and alteration of lysosomal enzyme activity.

D001840.s: An adhesion procedure for orthodontic attachments, such as plastic dental crowns. This process usually includes the application of an adhesive material (dental cements) and letting it harden in-place by light or chemical curing.

D002346.s: The dilated portion of the common carotid artery at its bifurcation into external and internal carotids. It contains baroreceptors which, when stimulated, cause slowing of the heart, vasodilatation, and a fall in blood pressure.

D002416.s: Self report questionnaire which yields 16 scores on personality traits, such as reserved vs. outgoing, humble vs. assertive, etc.

e: Hereditary Motor and Sensory-Neuropathy Type II
Neuropathy, Type II Hereditary Motor and Sensory
Hereditary Type I Motor and Sensory Neuropathy
Hereditary Motor, and Sensory Neuropathy Type I
Neuropathy, Type I Hereditary Motor and Sensory
D002607.s: A hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy transmitted most often as an autosomal dominant trait and characterized by progressive distal wasting and loss of reflexes in the muscles of the legs (and occasionally involving the arms). Onset is usually in the second to fourth decade of life.

D002672.s: A child or adolescent who, when compared to others of the same age or experience, exhibits capability of high performance in intellectual, creative, or artistic areas, possesses an unusual capacity for leadership or excels in specific academic fields. (From PL 100-297, Sec. 4103, Definitions)

D002971.s: Congenital defect in the upper lip where the maxillary prominence fails to merge with the merged medial nasal prominences. It is thought to be caused by faulty migration of the mesoderm in the head region.

D003055.s: The electric response of the cochlear hair cells to acoustic stimulation.

D003129.s: Fleshy and reddish outgrowth of skin tissue found on top of the head, attached to the sides of the head, and hanging from the mandible of birds such as turkeys and chickens.

D003194.s: A self-learning technique, usually online, involving interaction of the student with programmed instructional materials.

D003950.s: Methods and procedures for the diagnosis of diseases or dysfunction of the urinary tract or its organs or demonstration of its physiological processes.

D004061.s: A salicylate derivative and anti-inflammatory analgesic with actions and side effects similar to those of aspirin.

D004429.s: A mobile chain of three small bones (incus; malleus; stapes) in the tympanic cavity between the tympanic membrane and the oval window on the wall of inner ear. Sound waves are converted to vibration by the tympanic membrane then transmitted via these ear ossicles to the inner ear.

D004494.s: Hospital department responsible for administering educational and training activities pertaining to health for patients and staff.

D006243.s: A sebaceous gland that, in some animals, acts as an accessory to the lacrimal gland. The harderian gland excretes fluid that facilitates movement of the third eyelid.

e: BIPAP Biphasic Intermittent Positive Airway Pressure
D007385.s: Application of positive pressure to the inspiratory phase when the patient has an artificial airway in place and is connected to a ventilator.

D008201.s: Dilatation of the intestinal lymphatic system usually caused by an obstruction in the intestinal wall. It may be congenital or acquired and is characterized by diarrhea; hypoproteinemia; peripheral and/or abdominal edema; and protein-losing enteropathies.

D008410.s: Muscles arising in the zygomatic arch that close the jaw. Their nerve supply is masseteric from the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve. (From Stedman, 25th ed)

D008924.s: Infestations with arthropods of the subclass acari, superorder Acariformes.

D009057.s: General or unspecified diseases of the stomatognathic system, comprising the mouth, teeth, jaws, and pharynx.

D009215.s: The smooth muscle coat of the uterus, which forms the main mass of the organ.

D009369.s: New abnormal growth of tissue. Malignant neoplasms show a greater degree of anaplasia and have the properties of invasion and metastasis, compared to benign neoplasms.

D009471.s: A syndrome characterized by acute optic neuritis; myelitis, transverse; demyelinating and/or necrotizing lesions in the optic nerves and spinal cord; and presence of specific autoantibodies to aquaporin 4.

D009916.s: Diseases of the bony orbit and contents except the eyeball.

D012075.s: A spontaneous diminution or abatement of a disease over time, without formal treatment.

D012149.s: Use of a device for the purpose of controlling movement of all or part of the body. Splinting and casting are fracture fixation.

D012930.s: Social structure of a group as it relates to the relative social rank of dominance status of its members. (APA, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 8th ed.)

D012985.s: Specifications and instructions applied to the software.

D013047.s: Animals or humans raised in the absence of a particular disease-causing virus or other microorganism. Less frequently plants are cultivated pathogen-free.

D013968.s: Spontaneously remitting inflammatory condition of the thyroid gland, characterized by fever; muscle weakness; sore throat; severe thyroid PAIN; and an enlarged damaged gland containing giant cells. The disease frequently follows a viral infection.

D014028.s: Contamination of the air by tobacco smoke.

D014723.s: A small bony canal linking the vestibule of the inner ear to the posterior part of the internal surface of the petrous temporal bone. It transmits the endolymphatic duct and two small blood vessels.

D016233.s: Active immunization where vaccine is administered for therapeutic or preventive purposes.

D016358.s: Identification of those persons (or animals) who have had such an association with an infected person, animal, or contaminated environment as to have had the opportunity to acquire the infection.

D016862.s: A well-circumscribed mass composed of tuberculous granulation tissue that may occur in the cerebral hemispheres, cerebellum, brain stem, or perimeningeal spaces. Multiple lesions are quite common. Management of intracranial manifestations vary with lesion site.

D016888.s: Acquired degenerative dilation or expansion (ectasia) of normal blood vessels, often associated with aging. They are isolated, tortuous, thin-walled vessels and sources of bleeding.

D017887.s: A calcification of the posterior longitudinal ligament of the spinal column, usually at the level of the cervical spine. It is often associated with anterior ankylosing hyperostosis.

D018217.s: A form of osteogenic sarcoma of relatively low malignancy, probably arising from the periosteum and initially involving cortical bone and adjacent connective tissue. It occurs in middle-aged as well as young adults and most commonly affects the lower part of the femoral shaft. (Stedman, 25th ed)

D018262.s: An adenocarcinoma characterized by the presence of varying combinations of clear and hobnail-shaped tumor cells. There are three predominant patterns described as tubulocystic, solid, and papillary.

D018288.s: An anaplastic, highly malignant, and usually bronchogenic carcinoma composed of small ovoid cells with scanty neoplasm. It is characterized by a dominant, deeply basophilic nucleus, and absent or indistinct nucleoli. (From Stedman, 25th ed; Holland et al., Cancer Medicine, 3d ed, p1286-7)

D018406.s: Biological properties, processes, and activities of viruses, including the interactions with the cells they infect.

D019687.s: A complication of obstetric labor in which the corpus of the uterus is forced completely or partially through the uterine cervix. This can occur during the late stages of labor and is associated with immediate postpartum hemorrhage.

D019773.s: A membrane on the vitreal surface of the retina resulting from the proliferation of one or more of three retinal elements: (1) fibrous astrocytes; (2) fibrocytes; and (3) retinal pigment epithelium.

D020504.s: Works consisting of lists of publications on a subject and that provide full annotated bibliographical information together with substantive summaries or condensations of the facts, ideas, or opinions presented in each publication listed. (From LC Subject Cataloging Manual)

D028661.s: Association with or participation in an act that is, or is perceived to be, criminal or immoral. One is complicitous when one promotes or unduly benefits from practices or institutions that are morally or legally suspect.

D031249.s: A rare form of non-Langerhans-cell histiocytosis (histiocytosis, non-langerhans-CELL) with onset in middle age.

D040861.s: The moral obligations governing the conduct of commercial or industrial enterprises.

D043925.s: Agents that induce or stimulate physiologic angiogenesis or pathologic angiogenesis.

D047929.s: Childbirth at the end of a normal duration of pregnancy, between 37 to 40 weeks of gestation or about 280 days from the first day of the mother's last menstrual period.

D053609.s: A general state of sluggishness, listless, or uninterested, with being tired, and having difficulty concentrating and doing simple tasks. It may be related to depression or drug addiction.

D055593.s: Structures, properties, and processes involving the inanimate matter of Earth.

D057191.s: Organizational development including enhancement of management structures, processes and procedures, within organizations and among different organizations and sectors to meet present and future needs.

D057766.s: A course or method of action selected to guide and determine present and future decisions.

D058015.s: The transfer of information from experts in the medical and public health fields to patients and the public. The study and use of communication strategies to inform and influence individual and community decisions that enhance health.

D058257.s: Sterile clothing worn during surgical procedures to protect the surgical site from sources of contamination.

D058671.s: Drugs that bind to and block the activation of adrenergic beta-1 receptors.

D058907.s: Compounds that bind to and stimulate adenosine A1 receptors.

D058998.s: Observation and acquisition of physical data from a distance by viewing and making measurements from a distance or receiving transmitted data from observations made at distant location.

D061028.s: Discrete spots in taut bands of muscle that produce local and referred pain when muscle bands are compressed.

D066256.s: Food prepared for consumption without exposure to heat.

D000068036.s: Book-length narratives told using a combination of words and sequential art, often presented in comic book style. from (Fletcher-Spear et al., ALA Review, Winter 2005)

D000074389.s: The ratio of the dose that produces toxicity to the dose that produces a clinically desired or effective response.

D000077803.s: A reference work containing a list of words related to the Greco-Roman World giving information about form, pronunciation, etymology, grammar, and meaning.

D000078064.s: Increase in body weight of the mother during the course of her pregnancy.

D000093562.s: Surgery to restore, reconstruct, or improve the shape or appearance of a damaged, misshapen, or missing penis due to injury, disease, or developmental abnormalities.

D000093683.s: Health system model designed to maximize value for patients. Value based healthcare often emphasizes better patient outcomes for healthcare cost through best practices (e.g., preventive screening, quality incentives).

D000093863.s: Spatial separation of housing within a geographic area based on racial, ethnic, nationality and other socioeconomic factors.

D000095223.s: A person having origins in any of the white racial groups of Europe, the Middle East and North Africa (https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/1997/10/30/97-28653/revisions-to-the-standards-for-the classification-of-federal-data-on-race-and-ethnicity).

e: Pregnancy at Age 35 Years or Older
D000099087.s: Pregnancy in women at least 35 years old at the time of delivery. This was formerly known as geriatric pregnancy.
